verdict: REVISE — Gate 3 NOT passed. The package set is unusually well-evidenced (I re-derived ~30 load-bearing claims from source and executed `preflight()`; the great majority verified exactly, including every line reference I spot-checked in writes.py, refusals.py, executions.py, runs.py, manifests.py, sessions.py, identity.py, setup.py, 0016, 0032, 0013, 0005, 0001, engine/manifest.py and engine/test_manifest.py). Ownership is genuinely single-owner and the mutation_check.py serialisation chain (WP-001→003→004→005) actually holds. But five issues block: one real B1 coverage gap excluded from every package on a premise I falsified; one headline acceptance criterion that cannot fail against pre-fix code; one package whose acceptance criteria are not executable as written; two unsequenced same-file collisions that breach hard constraint 7; and one criterion requiring a tool the repository does not have. These are correctable without re-planning — four are edits to acceptance criteria and sequencing, one adds a bind site to an existing package.
blocking_issues: B1 COVERAGE GAP — a third bind site is excluded from every package on a false premise. WP-003 out_of_scope states, and the integrated plan repeats verbatim, that `backend/doorway/manifests.py:99` is not a B1 site because `value` "reaches only dict members and string concatenation, never a psycopg parameter." Observed, traced end to end: manifests.py:99 is `value=body.get("value")` with no isinstance guard and no str() coercion; runs.py:128 calls `manifests.manifest_from(body)`; engine/run.py:172 places `"value": manifest.value` into the run row dict; runs.py:224 passes that through `engine_run.run_rows` into `run_tables["run"]`; runs.py:332 `_insert(request, "run", ...)`; runs.py:273-279 `_insert` builds `%(name)s` placeholders and passes `row` straight to `request.write`. A dict- or list-valued `value` in a POST /runs body therefore reaches psycopg as a bind parameter and produces exactly B1's "cannot adapt type 'dict'" 500. WP-003 excludes it by name, WP-004 excludes it by name, and the plan's validation strategy asserts there is "now exactly one" site binding outside Write.bind. Success criterion 1 (every defect maps to a package) is not met for B1: the boundary half of the fix leaves this path open, and only WP-003's classification floor would touch it — turning a 500 into a 400 without the field-naming refusal the package promises.

WP-005 — the headline acceptance criterion cannot fail against pre-fix code, so it validates nothing. It reads: "For a manifest with an unknown category, both POST /manifests/check and POST /runs return 409 with a non-empty reason. Demonstrated failing (IndexError) against pre-fix code." Observed: `bug_report.md` B5 itself labels this "Latent — not reachable today." engine/manifest.py:111-113 appends to `dropped` if and only if `not categories.knows(risk.category)`, which is precisely the condition under which `categories.key_for` raises UnknownCategory at manifests.py:167-170 and runs.py. So `checked.dropped` non-empty implies `reasons` non-empty, and the unknown-category request returns 409 correctly today (manifests.py:171-180). The criterion passes vacuously before and after the fix, and the "demonstrated failing" step is impossible. Only WP-005's secondary criterion (a unit-level test driving the empty-`reasons` path directly) is capable of discriminating.

WP-008 — the acceptance criteria are not executable as written, and two of them conflict. Criterion 1 asks a source-shape test to assert that no doorway module "composes a caller-supplied identifier" against the five snapshot/ruleset tables "without first resolving through `cw.run`"; criterion 3 requires that same test to pass for a hypothetical legitimate future consumer that does resolve first. Whether an identifier is caller-supplied, and whether resolution happened first, are dataflow and ordering properties that no text or regex check can decide, and the package names no mechanism (regex? AST? allowlist?). Observed precedent in this repository is far simpler: test_executions.py:421-424 is `assert "update cw.agreement" not in source`, and test_writes.py:182-199 is a regex count over `WRITES[key].sql`. Criterion 3 is additionally not a test at all — a hypothetical consumer cannot be executed. As written the implementer must invent both the rule and its mechanism, which is the definition of an unvalidatable package.

HARD CONSTRAINT 7 BREACH — two files can be mutated by concurrent packages with no sequencing between them. (a) `backend/engine/mutation_check.py`: WP-001 scope offers to "extract the exactly-once/named-test preflight check into a small shared helper importable by backend/engine/mutation_check.py", while WP-002 Branch B requires updating the engine row that pins the severity branch. WP-002's prerequisites are "none" and it is explicitly told to be "raised IMMEDIATELY and in parallel with WP-001". (b) `backend/doorway/db.py`: WP-006 lists db.py as READ ONLY in its target files, but its implementation notes and risks both authorise setting `application_name` on the pool (db.py:164-173) as the acceptance discriminator, while WP-011 Option B adds a `ROLE_TO_DB_ROLE` entry (db.py:65-72). WP-006's prerequisite is WP-003; WP-011's chain is WP-001→009→010. Nothing orders them, and WP-006 asks the implementer to "confirm no concurrent package touches it" — which WP-011 conditionally does.

WP-009 — the primary acceptance criterion depends on a tool the repository does not have. It requires "a type checker (mypy or pyright, whichever the repository already uses) reports no undefined name for `Database`." Observed: there is no pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, mypy.ini or pyrightconfig.json under `backend/`, no mypy/pyright string in any config file in the tree, and `backend/package.json` declares no devDependencies at all (its only dependency is @electric-sql/pglite). Adopting the criterion means introducing a type checker and its configuration into the repository — unstated new scope in a package whose objective is "comment and import changes only; no behavioural change." The package identifies the fallback (remove `from __future__ import annotations` as a probe; sessions.py:70 `def __init__(self, db: Database, ...)` then raises NameError at def time, which is genuinely discriminating), tells the author "say which one the package uses; do not leave it to the implementer" — and then leaves it to the implementer.

Correct the plan's validation-strategy sentence "of which there is now exactly one" to two. New acceptance criterion for WP-004: `POST /runs` with a dict-valued `value` returns 400 `rejected`, demonstrated failing against pre-fix code where it returns 500 `broke` (the failure mode differs from executions.py:174's, which yields a not-found — both belong in the same package because both are cured by the same imported helper). Replace WP-005's first acceptance criterion. Delete "for a manifest with an unknown category ... demonstrated failing (IndexError)" and promote the unit-level criterion to primary: a direct test of the refusal branch with `checked.dropped` non-empty and `reasons` empty (constructed by stubbing `categories.key_for` to succeed, or by calling the guarded expression directly) returns a 409 with a non-empty reason instead of raising IndexError. Retain a separate non-regression criterion that the genuine unknown-category path still returns 409 with the engine's own sentence — but label it non-regression, not proof of fix. Downgrade WP-007's claim about `0016_doorway_login.sql:45` from Observed to Inferred and make its verification a prerequisite. The package asserts the unconditional `grant cw_viewer, ... to cw_app` "writes pg_auth_members on every per-test rebuild" and hardens that into a pass/fail criterion ("A package that covers only the two named in bug_report.md does not satisfy this criterion"). PostgreSQL treats a redundant GRANT of an already-held role membership as a no-op with a NOTICE; if that holds on the target server version, the criterion mandates a new migration for a statement that never contends. The statement's unconditionality is Observed (0016:45, outside the DO block); its contention is not. Verify with a probe against the actual cluster before binding it.

Fix two line references and one stale number, all cheap. (a) WP-001 and the integrated plan cite the idempotent session deletes at "sessions.py:93 and :114"; they are at 93 and 112. (b) More consequentially, both deletes are the byte-identical string `delete from cw.session where expires_at <= %s`, so the obvious replacement pattern for the two repointed rows appears TWICE and `preflight()` rejects hits > 1 as loudly as hits == 0 (mutation_check.py:489-499 — verified). per_package_notes: WP-001 (mutation harness) — ACCEPT WITH CORRECTIONS. Strongest-evidenced package in the set; I reproduced its central claim exactly. Executing `doorway.mutation_check.preflight()` returns 5 entries over 4 distinct rows out of 36 MUTATIONS, matching the package's text word for word, and `main()` at mutation_check.py:506-513 prints "STALE CHECKS — nothing was run" and returns 1 before any mutation, so all 36 guarantees are indeed unevaluated. preflight()'s exactly-once rule (hits == 0 and hits > 1 both fail) verified at mutation_check.py:489-499. `backend/package.json` verified: verify → test:mutation → `node db/test/mutation-check.mjs && python engine/mutation_check.py && python doorway/mutation_check.py`; no root package.json. `engine/mutation_check.py` verified to define `main()` at line 530 and no `preflight()`. The delete-race row's retirement argument is sound: sessions.py:93 and :112 are both `delete from cw.session where expires_at <= %s`, idempotent, and the named test is absent. Corrections: prerequisite field vs. external blocker; line 114→112; the duplicate-pattern collision; S56→read the head; and the engine/mutation_check.py collision with WP-002.

WP-006 (B2 advisory) — ACCEPT WITH ONE CORRECTION. Verified: advisory.py:274 opens `with db.as_person(caller.person, caller.role) as request:`, the model call `judge_semantic_difference(baseline, compared)` is at 304 inside it, the insert at 306, and `TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 20` at advisory.py:74 with `urlopen(..., timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS)` at 174. db.py:182-206 confirms `as_person` holds `conn.transaction()` open across the yield, so a pooled connection sits idle-in-transaction for up to 20 seconds; db.py:164-173 confirms `max_size: int = 10` and `kwargs={"autocommit": True}` with no `application_name`. The validation discriminator this package adds — that `pg_stat_activity` alone cannot separate serving-pool backends from test connections, so the criterion would pass whether or not B2 is fixed — is the sharpest catch in the whole package set and should be preserved verbatim. The staleness decision is correctly framed as decide-and-record, and the insert genuinely stores `baseline_text`/`compared_text`, which supports the recommended answer. WP-007 (B9 role collisions) — ACCEPT WITH ONE CORRECTION. Verified: setup.py:34-55 `prepare()` issues `alter role cw_app login password` unconditionally on every call, and setup.py:43-52 is the verify-don't-rewrite model it should copy (reads `rolinherit` from pg_roles and raises a RuntimeError naming 0016). 0016_doorway_login.sql:41 `alter role cw_app noinherit` in the DO block's else branch, and 0016:44-47 the `grant cw_viewer, ... to cw_app` outside it, both verified. migrate.py:41-42, :63, :75 verified: ledger is `filename text primary key`, done-set read by filename, insert of `path.name` — no checksum, so the forward-only argument for a new migration rather than an in-place edit of applied 0016 is correct. Refusing to delete the serial second pass is right and well-argued. Correction: the contention claim for 0016:45 is Inferred, not Observed (redundant role GRANTs are typically no-ops); verify before binding it as a pass/fail criterion. Also resolve migration numbering against WP-011 deterministically.

WP-008 (B4 invariant test) — REVISE. The evidence is right and the deferral judgement is right. WP-009 (B8 comment + imports) — REVISE. All facts verified: app.py:133-140 has the six-line monotonic-clock rationale immediately above `"expiresInSeconds": length,`; sessions.py:75-77 confirms the move to `time.time()` with its own comment explaining why monotonic was wrong, so the app.py rationale is genuinely stale; sessions.py:32 `import threading` is unused; sessions.py:70 `def __init__(self, db: Database, ...)` annotates a name never imported, surviving only via `from __future__ import annotations` at line 28; db.py imports nothing from sessions.py (only contextlib, typing, psycopg, psycopg_pool), so the added import creates no cycle — that check is correct where WP-010 shows the identity.py equivalent is not. The mutation-guarded line must not move, correctly stated. Only defect: the type-checker criterion (blocking issue 5).

WP-010 (constants relocation) — ACCEPT. The cycle is real and correctly diagnosed: identity.py:47-48 imports `from doorway.db import Database` and `from doorway.sessions import EIGHT_HOURS, Sessions, parse_duration`, so importing identity into sessions closes a loop. LOOKUP_ROLE = "viewer" at identity.py:57 and LOOKUP_ACTOR = "__signin__" at identity.py:62, both used at identity.py:101/115/130 and both hardcoded — as a pair — at sessions.py:87, 112, 119, 130, 134 (ten literal occurrences at five call sites), exactly as stated. Option (b), moving them into sessions.py which identity.py already imports, is the smaller correct change and adds no module. The "either import order in a fresh interpreter" criterion is executable and discriminating. Insisting the rationale comments travel with the constants is right — they become load-bearing under WP-011.

WP-011 (A-1) — ACCEPT AS GATED; do not author as implementable. Every security claim verified. 0032_session_store.sql:28 `grant select, insert, delete on cw.session to cw_viewer;` and :30-32 `create policy viewer_manages_sessions on cw.session for all to cw_viewer using (true);`, with the header calling cw_viewer "the lookup role". 0001_foundation.sql:93-95 `cw.app_actor()` is the `current_setting('cw.actor', true)` missing_ok form, so the package's insistence on it over a bare `current_setting` is correct and non-obvious. 0013_administrator.sql:84-94 `cw.app_role()` is a CASE over `current_user` naming exactly six roles and returning NULL otherwise, and 0013:252-253 `create policy read_all on cw.account for select using (cw.app_role() is not null)` — so the Option B costing is right: a cw_lookup role reads NULL, fails the account read policy, and sign-in breaks at runtime after the migration lands. db.py:65-72 ROLE_TO_DB_ROLE and db.py:140-147 SilentlyRefused (raised only from the write path) confirm the branch-neutral acceptance argument. migrate.py's filename-only ledger confirms that `git status` proves never-committed, not never-applied — so contract assumption A4 is correctly downgraded. This package is correctly blocked on three owner decisions; the only additions needed are migration-number allocation and the db.py sequencing against WP-006.

WP-012 (RLS deferral) — ACCEPT. Justified deferral, not an omission. The blast-radius argument is verified: runs.py:264-334 `_insert`/`_store` implement content-addressed sharing with `on conflict do nothing` on all five shared tables and an explicit comment that there is deliberately NO read-then-skip guard because it would be a second copy of one rule — so a policy scoped through cw.run must admit rows reachable via any run the caller may see, and getting it wrong breaks sharing or reopens the leak. The gating open question (can these tables carry cw.run-scoped policies at all) is genuinely unresolved and correctly left so. Minor: drop or restate the WP-008 prerequisite on a package that is not implemented.

WP-013 (migration checksum deferral) — ACCEPT. Correctly registered as new scope rather than smuggled in. migrate.py:41-42, :63 and :75 verified exactly as cited: `create table if not exists cw.schema_migration (filename text primary key, applied_at ...)`, `select filename from cw.schema_migration` into a done-set, `insert ... values (%s)` with `path.name`. The consequence — an edited applied migration is invisible forever to every installation that already ran it — is Observed, and it is precisely what makes WP-011's Decision 2 unanswerable from git. Keeping the interim mitigation (query the ledger on every developer database) inside WP-011 rather than deferring it with the checksum work is the right split.
